wrongItems.problem: 年月 in 「母と二人で過ごした年月を振り返る」 is not forced to としつき — ねんげつ is at least as natural a reading in this exact frame (長い年月/過ごした年月 are routinely read ねんげつ). Nothing in the sentence disambiguates, so a learner typing としつき is guessing. Needs a context that pins the emotive reading (e.g. 「としつきが流れる」-type collocations still don't force it; better to rebuild around an unambiguous frame).

明後日 is read あさって by default; みょうごにち is the formal/business minority reading. 「明後日の午後に打ち合わせを行う予定です」 is polite but ordinary — あさって is the reading nearly every learner and native speaker would produce here. The sentence does not force みょうごにち (that needs a stiff announcement/legal register, e.g. 「明後日をもって受付を終了いたします」).

「海で釣を楽しみました」 is orthographically wrong: the activity noun is 釣り with okurigana. Bare 釣 only appears in compounds/signage (釣具, 釣禁止) and in running text is read as part of お釣り (change). As written the sentence is not correct modern Japanese and also fails to force つり = fishing.

zh copies the kanji into a false friend: 「我在小学课上学习了国语」— Chinese 国语 means Mandarin/the national language of China (or, in Taiwan usage, the Chinese-language subject), not the Japanese-language school subject that 国語 denotes here. A Chinese learner is taught exactly the wrong referent. Needs 日语课 / 日语(国语)课. The en is also clumsy ('I studied Japanese language class') — 'I studied Japanese in class at elementary school'.

minorItems.problem: 「静かなどこか」 is the wrong word order for the indefinite pronoun: Japanese puts the modifier after どこか — 「どこか静かなところへ旅行に行きたい」. Pre-modifying どこか with a な-adjective is marked/poetic at best and teaches learners a bad pattern. Reading and grammar otherwise fine.
「独特な香りを持っています」 is translationese; a dish does not 香りを持つ in natural Japanese. Standard: 「この料理は独特の香りがします」 or 「独特の香りがある」. 独特の is also the commoner form before a noun. Reading どくとく is forced.

「胃の中で食物を適切に消化する。」 has no subject and uses an active transitive verb with no agent, so it reads as a sentence fragment/instruction. Natural: 「食物は胃の中で適切に消化される。」 The technical register does support しょくもつ over たべもの, so the reading is OK.

Word choice: 「大気がきれいになった」 is odd — 大気 is the atmosphere as a whole and collocates with 大気汚染; for local air becoming clean Japanese uses 空気. Natural: 「工場が減って空気がきれいになった」 or 「大気汚染が改善した」. Also 「工場の減少で」 is stiff nominalization for a spoken-register sentence.
Collocation is off: 「願いを込める」 needs a vessel to put the wish into (手紙に/贈り物に願いを込める). Wishing on a star is 「星に願いをかける」. 「星に自分の願いを込めた」 is understandable but not idiomatic.
「非常のとき」 is awkward. As a noun meaning emergency, 非常 lives in compounds and set phrases: 非常時には / 非常の際は / 非常の場合は. 非常のとき reads like a learner's construction; correct but unnatural.

Kanji choice for the sense: a manifestation of a feeling is conventionally written 感謝の表れ (NHK/press style reserves 現れ for things appearing physically). 現れ here is not flatly wrong but is the dispreferred spelling for exactly this 感謝の… context.

en and zh disagree on the same noun: 時計 is rendered 'a clock' in en but 一块手表 (a wristwatch) in zh. One of the two is wrong for the same jp word, and a learner comparing the two translations gets contradictory information about 時計.

Surrounding vocabulary above target level: 冷え込み (nominalized 冷え込む) is N2, and 冷え込みが激しい is a weather-report register. The target 近頃 is easy but the rest of the sentence is the hard part, so the drill trains an N2 collocation rather than the N3 adverb.

zh renders 鬼 as 鬼怪, which in Chinese reads as ghosts/spectres — the 恶鬼 sense the target is supposed to be distinguished from. en correctly says 'ogre'. 妖怪／(日本传说中的)鬼(食人怪) would carry the horned-ogre image the sentence and en both intend; 长着大角 only partly rescues it.

Both translations render 幅が狭い literally and end up unidiomatic. en 'The width of this road is very narrow' — a width is small/not narrow; should be 'This road is very narrow.' zh 「这条路的宽度非常狭窄」 has the same collocation clash (宽度…狭窄); 这条路非常窄 is what the jp means.

en and zh diverge on ゆっくり起きます. en 'I always get up slowly' is a literal misread (Japanese means getting up at a leisurely pace / sleeping in), while zh 「我总是很晚才起床」 says 'I always get up very late'. The two glosses teach different facts; en should be 'I always take my time getting up' or 'I always sleep in'.

misleadingCards.why: Sentence is 時計の針 = the hands of a clock, but the gloss line only offers "needle, pin". The clock-hand sense is absent, so the definition does not explain the sentence.
